pr.title: GH-139951: Fix major GC performance regression
pr.body:
This PR:

* Counts number of actually tracked objects, instead of trackable objects. This ensures that untracking tuples has the desired effect of reducing GC overhead
* Does not track most untrackable tuples during creation. This prevents large numbers of small tuples causing excessive GCs.

For the [example in the original report](https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/139951#issue-3505571273) this makes performance on main a bit better than 3.13.

Benchmarking results show this is about neutral on performance otherwise. 

<!-- gh-issue-number: gh-139951 -->
* Issue: gh-139951
<!-- /gh-issue-number -->

@@ -0,0 +1,7 @@
+Fixes a regression in GC performance for a growing heap composed mostly of
+small tuples.
+
+*  Counts number of actually tracked objects, instead of trackable objects.
+   This ensures that untracking tuples has the desired effect of reducing GC overhead.
+*  Does not track most untrackable tuples during creation.
+   This prevents large numbers of small tuples causing excessive GCs.

Do we really want to change `heap_size` here? Or maybe it'll be better to rename this to something like `all_count`?

IIUC, `assess_work_to_do` set `gc.young.count` to zero and if in `untrack_tuples` we untrack some tuples we don't decrease counter in `_PyObject_GC_UNTRACK`. On my sight, it is not very correct, but this gives us some room to subsequent trackings. 

I'm not sure we should address this in this PR, but I think I should say this.

IMO, we need test on this. I've created a separate PR to add it:
https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/140304
I've merged that PR.

The "heap size" is the count of all tracked object, so we do need to decrement it here.

We could make this more efficient, by only updating the heap size during GC, but I want to keep the changes small for the backport.

`untrack_tuples` untracks by calling `_PyObject_GC_UNTRACK` which will update the counts.
It might result in `gc.young.count` going negative, but that should only delay the next collection a bit, not have any effect on correctness.
